text: A vector is fixed precisely when ρ(m)=m⊗1, the coaction criterion of [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). The native statement only needs a coalgebra with a distinguished element called 1; it does not presume a multiplication or that this element is group-like. In the coordinate-Hopf-algebra case, this recovers scheme-theoretic invariants. Checks pass: [fixedSubcomodule_eq_top_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L81), [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L93).
Checks all vectors are fixed exactly when the fixed subcomodule is full.
Checks fixedness is preserved by comodule morphisms.

A comodule morphism sends a vector satisfying ρ(m)=m⊗1 to another satisfying the same equation. Apply f⊗id to the coaction equation and use colinearity. This is functoriality of the invariants described in [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107); preservation needs neither flatness nor injectivity, even over a commutative semiring. Checks pass: [fixedMap_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L105), [fixedMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L118).
Checks the induced invariant map has the original vector value.
Checks restriction to fixed vectors respects composition.

The induced map between fixed submodules evaluates as the original comodule morphism on underlying vectors. The restricted codomain is legitimate because colinearity preserves ρ(m)=m⊗1. This implements the invariants of [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107) without modifying the map or choosing a projection onto invariants; no splitting or exactness is asserted. Checks pass: [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L93), [fixedMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L111).
Checks the required target membership.
Checks the identity restriction.

If a direct-sum decomposition has every piece preserved by the coaction, each component of a fixed vector is fixed. The component projection commutes with ρ, so it preserves the equation in [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). Preservation of every piece is an explicit hypothesis; an arbitrary grading or decomposition does not suffice. Checks pass: [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L93), [symmetricAlgebraCoact_mem_decomposeTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/SymmetricAlgebra/Basic.lean#L248).
Checks fixedness under colinear maps.
Checks the actual homogeneous symmetric-algebra family satisfies the preservation hypothesis.

Over a commutative ring, an injective comodule morphism reflects as well as preserves fixedness when C is flat. Flatness makes f⊗id_C injective, allowing cancellation in the equation ρ(m)=m⊗1 from [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). The tensor-injectivity hypothesis is substantive; ordinary injectivity of f alone is not silently treated as sufficient. Checks pass: [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L93), [fixedMap_injective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L126).
Checks the forward preservation direction without flatness.
Checks injectivity of the restricted map on invariants.

This predicate asks for a nonzero vector v with ρ(v)=v⊗1, matching the fixed-vector criterion of [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). Nonzero is explicit, so the zero vector cannot satisfy the existence claim. The native field-coalgebra formulation uses a distinguished 1 and does not itself assume a group or prove such a vector exists. Checks pass: [hasNonzeroFixedVector_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Flag/Induction.lean#L67), [hasNonzeroFixedVector_iff_fixedSubcomodule_ne_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Flag/Induction.lean#L74).
Checks the exact existential definition.
Checks equivalence with a nonzero fixed subcomodule.

Unfolding the predicate yields exactly a vector v≠0 satisfying ρ(v)=v⊗1. This is an existential property, not a selected vector or a universal assertion about all representations. It expresses the nontriviality of the invariant space in [Milne 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107), under the native field and distinguished-element assumptions. Checks pass: [hasNonzeroFixedVector_iff_fixedSubcomodule_ne_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Flag/Induction.lean#L74), [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L75).
Checks the invariant-space interpretation.
Checks the underlying fixed-vector equation.

The c-weight space is the equalizer of ρ and m↦m⊗c, so it contains exactly the vectors transforming with that coefficient. This is [Milne 4.22](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103) in coaction form. The supplied c is bundled with Δ(c)=c⊗c and ε(c)=1; the resulting submodule may be zero and need not be one-dimensional. Checks pass: [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L79), [weightSubcomodule_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L93).
Checks the defining coaction equation.
Checks the stable subobject has exactly this carrier.

Membership in the c-weight space is precisely ρ(m)=m⊗c, because its carrier was defined as an equalizer of linear maps. This matches [Milne 4.22](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103), with c already certified group-like. Zero belongs to every weight space; distinct weights become distinguishable through a nonzero vector only with the appropriate cancellation hypotheses. Checks pass: [mem_weightSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L99), [coact_eq_tmul_of_mem_span](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L87).
Checks the identical equation for the stable-subobject packaging.
Checks scalar multiples keep the same coefficient.

A comodule morphism preserves each specified weight: applying f⊗id to ρ(m)=m⊗c yields ρ(f(m))=f(m)⊗c. This is functoriality of the spaces in [Milne 4.22](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103). The image vector may become zero; preserving membership does not mean preserving a nonzero weight vector or giving an isomorphism of weight spaces. Checks pass: [map_groupLikeWeightSpace_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L124), [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L79).
Checks inclusion of the entire image weight space.
Checks the equation used to identify the weight.

A vector has weight c exactly when every contraction T_φ of its coaction acts on it as multiplication by φ(c). This tests the equation of [Milne 4.22](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103) against all coefficient functionals. Projectivity of C ensures those contractions detect tensor equality; no projectivity or finite generation of M is required. Checks pass: [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L79), [tensor_eq_of_forall_tensorComponent_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean#L56).
Checks the tensor equation being detected.
Checks equality detection for a projective right tensor factor.

A one-dimensional subcomodule over a field lies in the weight space of a unique group-like element, as the character-on-a-line discussion in [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103) predicts. Choose a nonzero spanning vector; the coaction laws identify its coefficient as group-like, and a normalized functional proves uniqueness. No finite-dimensionality of the whole ambient comodule is assumed. Checks pass: [exists_isGroupLikeElem_coact_eq_tmul_of_toSubmodule_eq_span](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L146), [eq_of_coact_eq_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L122).
Checks existence of the group-like coefficient.
Checks uniqueness from the nonzero spanning vector.

The c-weight space equals the intersection of the eigenspaces of every contraction T_φ, with eigenvalue φ(c). Thus the coaction equation of [Milne 4.22](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103) becomes simultaneous linear equations. The coefficient coalgebra is projective over a commutative ring so its dual detects tensors; no simultaneous-diagonalization or spanning assertion is made. Checks pass: [mem_groupLikeWeightSpace_iff_forall_coactComponent_eq_smul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L162), [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L79).
Checks the elementwise simultaneous-eigenvector characterization.
Checks the original coaction definition.

Distinct group-like weight spaces form an independent family: each meets the sum of the others only in zero, generalizing [Milne 4.25](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=104). Here the base is a domain, M is torsion-free and C is projective. Dual functionals distinguish weights and joint-eigenspace independence applies; the theorem does not claim the spaces span M. Checks pass: [weightSpace_eq_iInf_eigenspace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L219), [finite_setOf_groupLikeWeightSpace_ne_bot_of_fg](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L271).
Checks the joint-eigenspace realization.
Checks its finite-support consequence when the supremum is finitely generated.

This predicate exhibits v≠0 and a group-like coefficient c with ρ(v)=v⊗c, the character-vector equation of [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103). Over a general commutative semiring, group-likeness is required explicitly rather than inferred from a nonzero vector. The definition states existence of one such vector, not a decomposition of the comodule. Checks pass: [hasNonzeroWeightVector_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L79), [hasNonzeroWeightVector_iff_exists_groupLikeWeightSpace_ne_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L131).
Checks the explicit nonzero and group-like requirements.
Checks equivalence with a nonzero group-like weight space.

Unfolding the weight-vector predicate produces v≠0, Δ(c)=c⊗c, ε(c)=1 and ρ(v)=v⊗c. These are the explicit coalgebra conditions behind the character-line description in [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103). The equivalence does not supply a canonical witness, infer group-likeness over arbitrary semirings, or require ambient finite-dimensionality. Checks pass: [hasNonzeroWeightVector_iff_exists_groupLikeWeightSpace_ne_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L131), [coact_eq_tmul_of_mem_span](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L87).
Checks the equivalent nonzero-weight-space formulation.
Checks the resulting coefficient persists on scalar multiples.

Every scalar multiple of a vector satisfying ρ(v)=v⊗c satisfies the same equation, by linearity and tensor scalar balance. This is the stable-line mechanism of [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103). Over the stated semiring, the singleton span is cyclic; neither v≠0 nor group-likeness of c is needed for this implication. Checks pass: [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L79), [hasNonzeroWeightVector_of_toSubmodule_eq_span](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L157).
Checks the interpretation when c is group-like.
Checks the converse stable-line mechanism under its stronger hypotheses.

For v≠0 with ρ(v)=v⊗c, the counit and coassociativity laws force ε(c)=1 and Δ(c)=c⊗c. A functional with φ(v)=1 cancels v. This explains the group-like character coefficient of [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103); the native theorem assumes a semifield and projective M, precisely supporting that normalized functional. Checks pass: [eq_of_coact_eq_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L122), [exists_isGroupLikeElem_coact_eq_tmul_of_mem_range](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L133).
Checks cancellation also gives uniqueness of the coefficient.
Checks the stable-line application.

A nonzero vector cannot have two different coefficients c and d in its coaction. Apply a functional normalized by φ(v)=1 to v⊗c=v⊗d to recover c=d. This justifies uniqueness in the character-line picture of [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103), under the native semifield and projective-module hypotheses; c and d need not be assumed group-like. Checks pass: [isGroupLikeElem_of_coact_eq_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L100), [existsUnique_le_groupLikeWeightSpace_of_finrank_eq_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Space.lean#L190).
Checks the coaction laws also force group-likeness.
Checks the resulting uniqueness for a line subcomodule.

If ρ(v) lies in the image of the tensor product of the cyclic span of v with C, it can be written v⊗c. For v≠0, the semifield and projectivity hypotheses then force c to be group-like. This gives the coefficient of a stable line in [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103), without treating tensor images as embeddings. Checks pass: [isGroupLikeElem_of_coact_eq_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L100), [exists_isGroupLikeElem_coact_eq_tmul_of_toSubmodule_eq_span](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L146).
Checks the recovered coefficient is group-like.
Checks application to an actual stable subobject.

A subcomodule whose underlying module is generated by v≠0 supplies a group-like c with ρ(v)=v⊗c. Stability puts ρ(v) in the cyclic tensor image; the semifield and projective-ambient-module hypotheses then identify c. This matches the character-line description of [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103), with no finite generation assumption on the ambient module. Checks pass: [exists_isGroupLikeElem_coact_eq_tmul_of_mem_range](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L133), [eq_of_coact_eq_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L122).
Checks the tensor-image step.
Checks the coefficient is uniquely determined.

A nonzero generator of a cyclic subcomodule witnesses that the ambient comodule has a nonzero group-like weight vector. The preceding coefficient construction supplies c and both group-like identities. This implements the stable-line picture of [Milne §4.g](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=103), retaining the semifield and projective-ambient-module assumptions needed to cancel the generator. Checks pass: [exists_isGroupLikeElem_coact_eq_tmul_of_toSubmodule_eq_span](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L146), [hasNonzeroWeightVector_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Weight/Vector.lean#L79).
Checks the actual group-like coefficient witness.
Checks that the supplied data meet the predicate exactly.

Given complementary stable submodules W and Q, projection along Q is a colinear endomorphism: it fixes W and kills Q, and stability makes both rules compatible with the coaction. This is the conditional direct-summand setting of [Milne §4.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). The complement is supplied; no semisimplicity, orthogonality or flatness is asserted. Checks pass: [projection_apply_of_mem_left](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L76), [projection_apply_of_mem_right](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L82).
Checks the projection fixes W.
Checks it vanishes on the supplied complement Q.

Projection onto W along its supplied stable complement Q always takes values in W. The map remains an endomorphism of the ambient module, so the theorem records membership rather than changing its codomain. This is the direct-summand projection associated with [Milne §4.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101), requiring a complement, not an inner product. Checks pass: [projection_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L62), [projection_apply_of_mem_left](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L76).
Checks it is the ordinary linear projection.
Checks vectors already in W are fixed.

Projection onto W along a complementary stable Q fixes every vector already in W, since its unique decomposition is v=v+0. This is the defining behavior of the direct-summand projection in the setting of [Milne §4.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). Complementarity means W∩Q=0 and W+Q=V; no orthogonality or existence of complements is inferred. Checks pass: [projection_apply_of_mem_right](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L82), [projection_apply_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L70).
Checks the complementary summand is killed.
Checks arbitrary outputs lie in W.

A strictly positive real exponent preserves strict order between nonnegative real bases. The smaller base may be zero: its power is then zero, while the larger positive base has a positive power. The exponent must be positive; exponent zero collapses both powers to 1, and negative exponents reverse order on positive bases. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L538).

A nonnegative real exponent preserves weak order between nonnegative real bases. It is enough to assume the smaller base is nonnegative, since the larger base then is too. Zero bases and exponent zero are permitted; the latter sends every base to 1. Consequently, this statement does not promise a strict inequality when the bases differ. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L550).

For a positive real exponent, comparing powers of two nonnegative real numbers is equivalent to comparing the bases. Thus the power both preserves and reflects weak order, including at zero. Positivity of the exponent is stronger than nonnegativity here: exponent zero gives equal powers for every pair and cannot recover the original comparison. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L574).

A nonpositive real exponent reverses weak order between positive real bases. The smaller base must be strictly positive; allowing zero would fail, for example because 0^(−1)=0 while 1^(−1)=1 in Lean. Exponent zero is included and makes both powers 1. The positivity hypothesis therefore concerns the bases, not the exponent. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L565).

For a real base at least 1, increasing the real exponent cannot decrease its power. Exponents may be negative, zero, or positive. At base 1 every power is 1, so the conclusion is deliberately a weak inequality. For a base strictly between zero and 1, the direction of comparison would instead reverse. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L617).

For a positive real base at most 1, increasing the real exponent cannot increase its power. All real exponents are allowed, and base 1 gives equality. Zero is excluded for a substantive reason: with Lean’s zero-power defaults, increasing the exponent from −1 to 0 changes the value from zero to 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L643).

A nonnegative real base strictly below 1 has power strictly below 1 for every positive real exponent. Zero is allowed and its power is zero. Both strict conditions matter for this conclusion: base 1 gives power 1, and exponent zero gives 1 even at base zero under Lean’s convention. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L658).

A real base between zero and 1, inclusive, raised to a nonnegative real exponent stays at most 1. Both endpoints and exponent zero are included. In particular, 0^0=1, while positive powers of zero are zero. The result is a weak upper bound; it does not assert that the power is strictly below 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L662).

A real base strictly greater than 1 raised to a negative real exponent is strictly below 1. The value is still positive, since the base is positive. This is the reciprocal-power behavior familiar from ordinary analysis. Exponent zero or base 1 would instead give equality, explaining the strict hypotheses. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L666).

A real base at least 1 raised to a nonpositive real exponent is at most 1. This includes equality at base 1 or exponent zero. All bases under consideration are positive, so no zero-power default is involved. The statement gives a weak upper bound without claiming that the result must be strictly smaller than 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L670).

A real base strictly greater than 1 raised to a positive real exponent is strictly greater than 1. This follows by comparing its base with 1 under a positive power. Neither strict condition can be relaxed while preserving this conclusion: base 1 or exponent zero makes the power exactly 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L674).

A real base at least 1 raised to a nonnegative real exponent is at least 1. Fractional exponents and exponent zero are allowed, as is base 1. The weak inequality accommodates these equality cases; it should not be read as a statement that taking a nonnegative power always strictly enlarges the base. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L678).

For a fixed positive real base different from 1, equal powers have equal real exponents, and conversely. Bases greater than 1 give a strictly increasing function of the exponent; bases between zero and 1 give a strictly decreasing one. Base 1 is excluded because all its powers coincide, so it cannot distinguish exponents. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L924).

For a fixed nonzero real exponent, equal powers of two nonnegative real bases imply equal bases, and conversely. Negative exponents and a zero base are allowed: zero’s assigned power is zero, whereas positive bases have positive powers. This is injectivity, not global order reversal for negative exponents when zero is included. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L767).

For a nonnegative real base and a nonzero real exponent y, first taking the power 1/y and then the power y recovers the base. Negative y and a zero base are allowed under Lean’s finite zero-power defaults. The reciprocal exponent uses real arithmetic; y=0 is excluded because the composition would then be constantly 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L506).

For a nonnegative real base, taking a nonzero real power y and then the power 1/y returns the original value. The reciprocal is computed in the real numbers, and y may be negative. Nonnegativity of the base matters: squaring a negative number and taking its nonnegative square root recovers its absolute value instead. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L503).

For a nonnegative real x and a nonzero natural n, raising x to the ordinary nth power and then to real exponent 1/n returns x. The natural n is cast to the reals before inversion, so 1/2 means one half, not zero. The base restriction selects the nonnegative root and prevents sign loss for even n. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L509).

For a nonnegative real x and a nonzero natural n, the real power x^(1/n), raised to the ordinary nth power, equals x. The reciprocal is taken after casting n to the reals, so it represents the usual root exponent. Zero bases are included; n=0 is excluded because it would yield the constant value 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L513).

Lean’s real square root equals the real power with exponent one half for every real input. For nonnegative inputs this is the usual nonnegative square root. For negative inputs both sides are assigned zero: square root clips negative inputs to zero, while real exponentiation takes the real part of the principal complex square root. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L990).

For a nonnegative real x and any real r, x^(r/2) equals (√x)^r. The division r/2 is real division, so fractional and negative exponents are retained exactly. Zero is allowed under Lean’s power defaults. The base condition matters: for x=−1 and r=2, the left side is −1 but the right side is zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean#L998).

For a quasi-coherent module sheaf F on any scheme X and any affine open U, Hⁿ⁺¹(U,F)=0 for every natural number n. The cohomology is that of the underlying abelian sheaf on the Zariski site; “Subsingleton” means its group is zero. No Noetherian or finite-generation assumption is present, and degree zero is excluded. See [Stacks, Lemma 30.2.2 (01XB)](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XB). Check *test_affine_vanishing* passes through [the computed two-basic-open family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/Affine.lean#L89) and [finite-cover exactness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/Affine.lean#L225).
The actual finite basic-open covers have exact augmented Čech complexes
Two-open exactness uses the actual difference of restrictions
Sections on a basic open extend after multiplication by a power

For any commutative ring R, every quasi-coherent module sheaf on Spec R has zero cohomology in every positive degree. The conclusion uses ordinary Zariski sheaf cohomology; “Subsingleton” means the zero additive group. The degree n+1 excludes H⁰, which remains global sections. Neither Noetherianity nor finite generation is assumed; the zero ring is allowed. See [Stacks, Lemma 30.2.2 (01XB)](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XB). Check *test_affine_vanishing* passes via [the whole-space comparison and affine theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/Affine.lean#L254); [H⁰ agrees naturally with global sections](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/Basic.lean#L85).
Whole-space affine vanishing uses the actual H′ to H comparison
Degree zero remains the global-sections functor, naturally
